doc.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022

title: Getting students playing outside school: Taps and the World Band
summary: He involves students in Taps Across America and the World Band for the Song for Hope documentary, likening it to childhood talent shows.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: got them hooked, and I’ll share one other thing, and I hope I’m not just going on and on — running on here. Okay? What I’d like to do is get students involved in things in addition to their school musical activities. Give you a good example: Trumpet players, would you like to be part of Taps Across America on Veteran’s Day or Memorial Day? You’ll be seen on YouTube, blah-blah-blah. Okay? We get them to play “Taps.” We did a thing with the World Band for a documentary that I’m involved in, an award-winning documentary, they’ve won in Barcelona and in Charleston already. That documentary is called “Song for Hope.” It’s about Ryan Anthony, the late Ryan Anthony, the great Ryan Anthony and his cancer and developing “Cancer Blows” which all these trumpet players are involved in. Okay? But they did a thing with the World Band. And, “Would you like to be in the World Band? You’re going to be part of 1,300 musicians, pros, young players, classical players, whatever.” And you get them involved in something outside of just a school environment. It’s an amplification of it. The other thing about that, when we talked about jazz improv before, we talked about the hesitation and the trepidation, you know, to go ahead and play, right? Well they make their videos and they go out and they’re performing. It’s no different than the talent shows that Jai Florada and I used to do when we were young kids. They used to take us around to the talent shows. You know?
You’ve come a long way, baby.
